english_explanations: The science of ancient life through fossil animals and plants.
example_sentences: Paleontology traces the ancestry of the elephants.

english_explanations: A scientist who studies the biology of extinct organisms.
example_sentences: The paleobiologist dated the mammoth bones with isotopes.

english_explanations: The earliest period of the Mesozoic era, about 252 to 201 million years ago.
example_sentences: The first dinosaurs appeared in the Triassic.

english_explanations: The middle period of the Mesozoic era, about 201 to 145 million years ago.
example_sentences: Giant sauropods dominated the Jurassic landscape.

english_explanations: The last period of the Mesozoic era, ending 66 million years ago in a mass extinction.
example_sentences: The Cretaceous ended with the dinosaurs' extinction.

english_explanations: The epoch of repeated ice ages, from about 2.6 million to 11,700 years ago.
example_sentences: Mammoths roamed the Pleistocene steppe.

english_explanations: A division of geological time; a distinctive period in history.
example_sentences: The fossils date from a warmer epoch.

english_explanations: Periods of a thousand years (singular: millennium).
example_sentences: The tortoises colonized the islands millennia ago.

english_explanations: A sequence of descendants traced from a common ancestor.
example_sentences: DNA shows the finches share one lineage.

english_explanations: A population within a species that differs in genetics or appearance.
example_sentences: Each island hosts its own subspecies of the lizard.

english_explanations: An animal lacking a backbone, such as an insect or worm.
example_sentences: Owls feed on invertebrates after dark.

english_explanations: An animal with a backbone, including fish, birds, and mammals.
example_sentences: Fish, birds and mammals are all vertebrates.

english_explanations: To dig out something buried, especially archaeological remains.
example_sentences: Workers excavated bear bones from the cave floor.

english_explanations: To find by digging; to reveal something hidden.
example_sentences: Speleologists unearthed cave-bear skulls in the alpine cave.

english_explanations: A dense metal rare on the surface, concentrated by asteroid impacts.
example_sentences: The iridium layer marks the dinosaurs' demise.

english_explanations: A naturally magnetic iron ore; birds may use it to sense direction.
example_sentences: Beak cells contain magnetite, a built-in compass.

english_explanations: A form of an element with a different atomic weight, used to date and trace remains.
example_sentences: Isotopes in bones reveal what the cave bears ate.

english_explanations: An instrument that analyses light or mass to identify substances.
example_sentences: The team ran the samples through a mass spectrometer.

english_explanations: The destruction or killing of a large proportion of a group.
example_sentences: Otters suffered decimation during the fur-trade years.

english_explanations: Killing far beyond what is sustainable; a proposed cause of megafaunal extinction.
example_sentences: Human overkill may explain the mammoths' disappearance.

english_explanations: To cause severe and lasting damage to something.
example_sentences: A flood devastated the ants' nest galleries.

english_explanations: To return a species, often captive-bred, to its former wild habitat.
example_sentences: Otters were reintroduced to the river after decades of absence.

english_explanations: Tourism to natural areas designed to support conservation.
example_sentences: Ecotourism now funds the monkey reserve.

english_explanations: A person who works to protect wildlife and habitats.
example_sentences: Conservationists campaigned to save the thylacine, but too late.

english_explanations: (of animals) born and raised in captivity, often for release into the wild.
example_sentences: Captive-bred ferrets learned to hunt before release.

english_explanations: The state of a species having no living members.
example_sentences: The flightless bird slid into extinction within decades.
